body:
Highlight builtin diffs with treesitter. Create an opt-in plugin, enabled `:packadd nvim.diffhl`. To load queries conditionally and properly, use custom pack-path plugin. Alternatives include a custom treesitter predicate `diffhl`, defining queries inline or creating a `runtime/queries/diff/diffhl.lua`. Do not define new highlight groups - rather, further specify `@diff.{minus,plus}.diff` if the plugin is enabled. This + the opt-in nature of the plugin grants colorscheme authors the ability to "catch up" and define these groups. The highlighting responds well to toggles of `termguicolors` and `background`. It looks like this OOTB: ## Addendum: The `'termguicolors'` Situation is Insane `notermguicolors` limits our choice of colors. I chose a light bg yielding:
Show image
If we set a dark bg, the default colorscheme overlaps and characters, like strings, become "invisible" (same fg & bg).

comment_data.body:
The `Diff*` highlight groups are for `:h diff-mode`, so the naming doesn't quite fit here.
The `diff*` (and as far as I understand `@diff.*`) highlight groups are for diff patches.

If I understand this correctly, the most fitting solution here is for queries to just use `@diff.plus` and `@diff.minus` captures. This approach:
- Doesn't require new special highlight groups.
- By default would use the already defined diff-patch tree-sitter highlight groups, which would highlight foreground as green and red.
- Opens the door for the user to override as `@diff.plus.diff` and `@diff.minus.diff` to have green and red background if they want to show syntax highlighting in diffs. Those groups also may or may not be defined by the default color scheme in this way.

comment_data.body:
Following [this discussion](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/40851#discussion_r3789120471), I still think that defining these groups in default color scheme is a bad idea, assuming the currently laid out workflow of "opt-in via enabling tree-sitter".

The main culprit is that this will immediately break virtually all color schemes in diff files with tree-sitter enabled. Here is what will happen:
- If color scheme does nothing, then `+` / `-` lines will be highlighted with green / red colors that don't match the color scheme. Which usually leads to readability issues, not even mentioning the aesthetic reasons. So color schemes *must* do something here. Which is already bad, especially since color schemes are not the most active plugins.
- It is not quite possible for the color scheme to support both "without injections" and "with injections" use cases. Since the first is usually highlighted via foreground and the second requires background highlighting. And color schemes don't know in advance which variant will be used.
- Also, a significant amount of color schemes don't have a dedicated "green/red background" color in their palette (like, for example, the whole `base16` approach). For `Diff*` groups they use green/red foreground color as background with regular background color as the foreground. So they in principle can't support "highlighted text with colored background" use case, as the foreground from the `@diff.{plus,minus}.diff` groups will be overridden by the injected syntax highlighting.

Sorry for the churn.

Can you please recap in terms of a) visible diff ui before and after (ie visual description of expected diff hl bg/fg before and after the plugin is enabled) and b) highlight groups (ie add X , Y, remove Z) what *you* think optimal API looks like? 

I see a lot of what _not_ to do - and this thread has been quite long - I'm not so sure what you're recommending in the affirmative?

Just want to be 100% sure I'm on the same page - sorry I missed this.

> Can you please recap in terms of a) visible diff ui before and after (ie visual description of expected diff hl bg/fg before and after the plugin is enabled) and b) highlight groups (ie add X , Y, remove Z) what _you_ think optimal API looks like?

See [this comment](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/40851#pullrequestreview-4946183505).

One of the main problems is that this is not a "plugin is enabled" type of design, but rather coupling this new highlighting with enabling tree-sitter highlighting. There are two (somewhat connected) groups of people that I think will be negatively affected by this:

- People who use a color scheme without a palette that has green/red for *background that displays syntax highlighted text*. It is quite often the case that colored background requires black/white foreground to keep text readable.
- People who want to use tree-sitter highlighting for `diff` filetype *but* without injected syntax highlighting. This is a reasonable use case because 1) green/red added/removed lines *is* already syntax highlighting for diff filetype; 2) tree-sitter highlighting based on an out-of-cotext text chunk is not always reliable. For these people clearing `@diff.{plus,minus}.diff` is not enough, they also need to deal with overriding bundled query file. Which is an extra (**undocumented** here) work and can be more nuanced that just putting an empty `queries/diff/injections.scm` (there might be other useful injections, like in 'nvim-treesitter').

> I see a lot of what _not_ to do - and this thread has been quite long - I'm not so sure what you're recommending in the affirmative?

If I had something actionable to suggest, I would have.

My best attempt is to somehow make this kind of highlighting fully opt-in: if user chooses to enable this, queries are added with `vim.treesitter.query.set()` and `@diff.{plus,minus}.diff` are created with `default=true` flag. Maybe only temporarily at least for a while until color schemes are caught up and users of diff tree-sitter highlighting are aware of this feature. Then it might be converted to opt-out and/or bundled as it is now. In other words, treat it like "plugin that can be enabled", as you described it earlier.
Just piping in to say I'd definitely belong in group 2: syntax highlighting diff files should be red/green, not injected.

What is the reasoning behind preferring "green on green" and "red on red" default highlights? I think this needlessly makes it harder to read. Using the most extreme grey of the opposite lightness will make it more readable.

comment_data.body:
> To load queries conditionally and properly, use a custom treesitter predicate `diffhl`. The alternatives are defining queries inline or creating a `runtime/queries/diff/diffhl.lua`. All approaches are novel.

Hard-coding filetype specific custom predicate in the core is arguably a more novel approach than listed above.

A less novel approach might be to put all this code inside `runtime/pack/dist/opt` for an opt-in plugin.

> What is the reasoning behind preferring "green on green" and "red on red" default highlights?

I naively follow the approach of almost every application I've seen with diff syntax highlighting - claude, codex, codeberg, forgejo, devin, etc. They all do this, with the notable exception being the platform we're on: GitHub.

I understand if we may depart from precedence here - but wondering if this sways you/would like some more intuition here (i.e. does our opinion of readability trump any existing precedence, and why).

Thanks for the quick review.

This change (including the already merged PR) has significant downstream implications, so I would appreciate it if we could take our time thinking through them before merging things. This also requires matching changes in nvim-treesitter, otherwise those queries shadow the ones here and people don't see anything (and complain).

I don't see any need to hurry here.
FYI: I'd probably document a way to disable the injection when one _is_ enabling Tree-Sitter for diffs.

> FYI: I'd probably document a way to disable the injection when one is enabling Tree-Sitter for diffs.

You can't (easily), same as any other bundled queries. This is why I keep saying this requires deliberation.
Great - I'll put up another PR with the nvim-treesitter queries _before_ anything related to this feature was added - so at least we can use the parser while it's bundled...

I would prefer to work on these queries in nvim-treesitter -- we have much better (more specific) CI there. I would also like to keep that as the record of truth without exception (for the same reason)  @ribru17 

(Note that for any change to the highlight groups, _this_ is the right repo, so those decisions should be made first.)

(It'll take another one or two weeks until I cut another diff parser release anyway, so we don't need to hurry there.)

> Also, the current implementation doesn't seem to 100% work after quick testing. Not all hunks have syntax highlighting. For example, this diff file has only the first hunk with syntax highlighting:

In that example, the diff is technically not syntactically correct (at least, in the eyes of tree-sitter). Context lines always need a preceding space character to be detected, if they're empty then they aren't parsed as part of the parent `hunk`. The space characters should always get inserted by `git --diff` thankfully (and `diff -u`)

So at least on "best effort basis" it would be better to support. And if "best effort basis" is "no support since the parser says so", then so be it :)

My two main concerns revolve around the opt-out design:
- There are non-trivial amount of color schemes that would not be able to support colored background with colored foreground. They would never work out of the box, which is bad and requires user to take extra action.
- It is not *quite* intuitive how to fully disable this, which should be documented with copy-pasteable code snippet.

To me a better approach would be an opt-in choice, described [here](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/40851#discussion_r4164470345).

A new iteration has been made (re-read the PR desc). I'd like to reach a compromise here as this is new territory for queries. 

Thanks everyone for your patience. A re-review is appreciated!

After moving to the opt-in `pack/dist/opt` package, this is a much lower risk than the initial forced approach. Whether the overall approach of tree-sitter injections being good enough for core is an open question. It *will* have highlighting issues due to lack of context, but not sure how severe.

> Now that the diff parser is bundled in core, shouldn't we do this anyways?

Normally not, since you may want pre-release updates or even a custom parser (with custom queries).

But, yes, I believe that this is a reasonable general recommendation: if you want to use the plugin, you _must_ use the bundled parser so should not install a third-party `diff` parser and queries.

And this call-out should absolutely be part of this PR as this is a serious footgun for users.
